issues_confirmed: Waitlist_Display_Chrome/content.js:130-137 - the hide path only removes the 'visible' class, which controls opacity/transform alone (CSS :49-52). The inline display='flex' set at :117 is never reverted (the restore is commented out at :133-136) and the base rule at :29-48 sets no pointer-events, so after the queue clears a position:fixed, opacity:0, z-index:99999 box stays hit-testable in the bottom-right corner of mindvideo.ai and silently eats clicks.

Waitlist_Display_Chrome/content.js:72 - the innerText fast-path guarding the DOM walk at :75 is permanently defeated once the badge renders, because the badge's own literal text ' Est. Wait: ' (built at :20) is inside document.body and innerText includes rendered (opacity:0 still counts) elements. Every debounced mutation batch then runs the full querySelectorAll('span, div, p, li') walk for the life of the page.

Waitlist_Display_Firefox/content.js:29-35 - updateTitle writes ORIGINAL_TITLE back unconditionally when no number is found. Chrome guards exactly this with lastTitle (:96, :125-127), restoring only if it set the title itself. mindvideo.ai is a Next.js SPA that sets document.title on route change, so the Firefox copy re-pins the tab to the document_idle title every 5s (:60) and on every mutation.

playback_speed_controller/content.js:344-358 - yts-saved-speed is applied once per script injection, via a 500ms setInterval that clearIntervals itself on finding a <video> and is abandoned after 10s (:356). The content script does not re-run on YouTube's History API navigation, so the restore fires only for the first video of the session.

playback_speed_controller/content.js:328-341 - the 1s interval reads video.playbackRate INTO the number input (:336) but never writes the saved speed back to the video, so the panel displays the reset rather than preventing it.

playback_speed_controller/content.js:180 + manifest.json:17 - createUI's only guard is the panel-exists check and the match pattern is *://*.youtube.com/* with no path restriction, so the panel is appended (:274) and visible by default (:195) over the homepage, search, subscriptions and history.

playback_speed_controller/content.js:180/:186/:274 - the existence guard precedes an await (chrome.storage.local.get) while appendChild is at :274, so two createUI calls inside that window both pass. Real but narrow: the only callers are a 1s interval (:329) and the toolbar message (:322), so the window is ~1ms. Consequences if hit: duplicate document keydown listeners from :293 (']' steps 0.2x) and an undismissable duplicate panel, since :312-320 only touches getElementById's first match.

Auto_Scroll_shorts/content.js:284 - tryClickNextOverlayButton is called from a bare setInterval every GOKU.overlayClickRetryMs=1300ms (:17, :275-285). Its guards at :194-195 are only enabled/isGokuSeriesPage/debounceReady; nothing checks currentTime, duration or ended. debounceReady needs 1200ms (:6) against a 1300ms poll, so it never throttles. On a series page with a visible 'Next Episode' control this clicks ~1.3s after arrival and chains through the series, undermining the correct ended/near-end listeners at :225-231.

Auto_Scroll_shorts/content.js:31 - the second clause (location.hostname !== 'www.youtube.com') is unreachable; /youtube\.com$/i already matches that host. :36's (^|\.)goku\.sx$ also accepts subdomains the manifest never injects into (manifest.json:8 is https://goku.sx/* only).
Auto_Scroll_shorts/manifest.json - no 'description' field, the only one of the five without one; shows blank in chrome://extensions.
Waitlist_Display_Chrome/service_worker.js - two comment lines stating no background logic is required, registered anyway by manifest.json:17-19. MV3 does not require a background entry.
Waitlist_Display_Firefox/manifest.json:18 - gecko id is still the placeholder queue-wait-tab-title@your-domain.com.
Waitlist manifests disagree on scope - Chrome matches all of https://www.mindvideo.ai/* (manifest.json:12), Firefox only /text-to-video/* (:11).
README.md:50 - install step names 'Waitlist Display Firefox' with spaces; e495b44 renamed it to Waitlist_Display_Firefox. This is the single instruction a new machine follows.
README.md:33-36 - documents a 'Remove Sponsors (Placeholder)' extension; no Remove_Sponsors/ exists in the tree and git cannot track an empty directory.
README.md:54-77 - a second TODO section that contradicts todo.md, still proposing the unified manager popup that todo.md dropped.
Ctrl_Click_New_Tab/content.js:45 - '[href]' in the fallback selector is redundant for anchors; a[href] is already consumed at :39-43, so it only ever catches non-anchor elements carrying an href.
playback_speed_controller/content.js:285 - rangeInput.value is only updated when speed <= 4, so above 4x the slider thumb no longer reflects the actual speed.

verdict: Nearly finished. 8cf9e9f closed the last outright-broken feature, so nothing here fails to do its job any more. What remains is one stale doc (the install step has been wrong for three cycles and is the only thing stopping someone else - or future-you on a new machine - from using this), three small bugs that are each under an hour, and one decision the owner can settle in a single browser tab. No dependency rot, no syntax rot, no scaffolding needed. Two or three focused sessions from genuinely done.
